html:
French general and statesman who led the Free French against Nazi Germany and later founded the Fifth Republic, serving as its president from 1959 to 1969.

He fought in the First World War and was wounded and captured at Verdun. When France fell in June 1940, he flew to London and, on 18 June, called on the French by BBC radio to fight on. He led Free France from abroad, refused to accept the Vichy regime, and in 1944 entered liberated Paris. He headed the provisional government until 1946.

In 1958 a crisis over the Algerian War brought him back. He wrote a new constitution with a strong president, the Fifth Republic, and in 1962 he let Algeria go to independence.

As president he pursued French independence and greatness: France built its own atomic bomb, left NATO's military command and was twice kept out of the European Economic Community by his veto on Britain's entry. Student and worker protests shook his rule in May 1968. He resigned in 1969 after losing a referendum and died the next year.
